summary: Create a board orchestration capability. The board owns cross-capability policy and composition; work-items and labels remain independent and expose narrow trusted server APIs.

tree.purpose: RSC route-private presentation; authenticates request context and calls the board RSC surface.
Framework-neutral orchestration: loads work items, removes archived items, obtains label details, rejects inaccessible label references, groups by status, and returns the board projection.
Board trusted server API; server-only composition root wiring board application dependencies to work-items and labels public server surfaces.
Current-request RSC read surface used by the board page; maps request identity and expected outcomes for RSC rendering.
Existing trusted server read API returning actor-scoped work items with label IDs; owns work-item persistence and ownership predicates.
Existing trusted server API returning label details only when the actor may view them, while distinguishing inaccessible references from absent labels.
Reusable board presentation, if the board view is part of the capability contract; receives only the board projection.
Application policy and failure-outcome tests with narrow capability fakes.
RSC integration tests for authentication, rendering, and channel-level failure behavior.

flows: `load-board` -> `work-items/server.ts`: fetch actor/tenant-scoped work items including status, archived state, and label IDs.
`load-board` filters archived items before deriving label IDs, then -> `labels/server.ts` with the remaining IDs and actor identity.
Labels returns visible details plus inaccessible-reference information; the board operation rejects the board result if any referenced label cannot be viewed.
`load-board` attaches visible label details and groups the resulting items by status, then returns a board projection to the RSC page.
The page renders `BoardView` or route-local markup from the projection; no page code imports store adapters or capability internals.

decisions.rationale: Filtering, grouping, label projection, authorization consequences, and cross-capability coordination survive deletion from the route, so the deletion test requires an orchestrating capability.

decisions.choice: Board depends on work-items and labels trusted server surfaces
decisions.rationale: Work-items and labels never import each other; the dependency graph remains acyclic and each capability retains persistence ownership.

decisions.choice: Fetch work items, filter archived items, then fetch labels
decisions.rationale: The second query depends on label IDs from the first and should avoid fetching labels for hidden archived items.

decisions.choice: Authenticate at the RSC/server boundary; enforce board policy in the application; enforce ownership/tenant predicates in each store
decisions.rationale: This separates request identity, board-specific rejection rules, and capability-owned data protection.

decisions.choice: Fail the board read on an inaccessible referenced label; report unexpected failures once at the RSC/channel boundary
decisions.rationale: A hidden label must not be silently exposed or silently omitted, while expected authorization/data outcomes remain typed and provider defects are not double-reported.

decisions.choice: Expose only `rsc.ts`/`server.ts` needed by current consumers
decisions.rationale: The page needs an RSC read surface; board server composition needs the trusted APIs. No actions, route handlers, client, stream, or job surface is required.
Coverage should verify archived filtering, grouping, label attachment, inaccessible-label rejection, auth, store scoping, and unexpected-failure handling without coupling to call-count details.

risks: The labels API must distinguish an inaccessible label from a nonexistent label; otherwise the board cannot enforce the required rejection policy reliably.
A label-provider outage or malformed trusted data should produce the board’s generic failure state and one report, with provider details redacted from the response.
Production build checks should enforce `server-only`/`client-only` boundaries and prevent browser code from importing `server.ts`, `rsc.ts`, or `server/**`.
